title: route-hash-entropy-split-from-nonstandard-header-encoding-and-rollout-mitigation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: During a staged model rollout to EU production we observed uneven traffic distribution across A/B variants caused by a previously unseen header encoding introduced by a downstream proxy. The mismatch produced divergent route-hash values resulting in >70% of traffic hitting Variant B and saturating its dedicated pool. Rollback attempts were partially blocked by a version-pinning edge case. This ticket tracks root cause, immediate mitigations, and follow-up hardening work.
detection: Automatic canary health checks raised elevated error rates for model variant B at 2026-03-10T08:14:00Z. Pager triggered and on-call responded within 6 minutes. Console route-split telemetry flagged abrupt weight shift from ~50/50 to ~10/90 across the AB route in EU region.
timeline:
2026-03-10T08:08Z - Canary rollout (traffic shift +10% -> 50%)
2026-03-10T08:14Z - Canary health alerts (5xx increase, tail latency spike)
2026-03-10T08:18Z - Ops investigation identifies route-hash skew for requests with X-Client-Meta header
2026-03-10T08:25Z - Attempted rollback (route update) partially failed due to version pinning on Variant B
2026-03-10T08:33Z - Temporary mitigation: network policy to strip X-Client-Meta applied at edge for EU
2026-03-10T09:02Z - Traffic returns to nominal distribution and error rates decline
2026-03-11 - Engineering postmortem investigation begins
2026-03-14 - Fix PRs opened and this ticket created to track follow-ups
impact: Affected ~1200 requests/min in eu-west; Variant B experienced 3x CPU utilization and 8% error rate for ~45 minutes. Two enterprise customers observed degraded latency for inference endpoints (SLO breaches for 35-minute window). No data exfiltration or model corruption.
root_cause: Route hashing function used a byte-level normalization that treated non-ASCII byte sequences introduced by a base64-like encoding in X-Client-Meta as distinct tokens. Downstream proxy started sending a compacted non-URL-safe base64 encoding which included padding variants and non-standard characters. The mismatch caused inconsistent canonicalization between the ingress proxy and the route-matcher, creating hash entropy in the route key space and sending disproportionate traffic to Variant B. Additionally, a version-pinning guard prevented full rollback because pinning metadata from an earlier canary run was left in the deployment record.
remediation: Short term: edge strip of X-Client-Meta for EU applied to normalize incoming requests and stop feeding anomalous keys to route-matcher. Manually unpinned variant B to allow rollback. Medium term: normalize header canonicalization in route-matcher and edge (reject or canonicalize nonstandard encodings). Long term: add deterministic route hashing tests and fuzzing for header encodings, and tighten rollout gating when redistribution occurs.
action_items: ENG-73109-A: Add canonicalization layer in route-matcher to UTF8-validate and reject non-URL-safe base64 payloads in routing keys (owner: Carlos Mendes, estimate: 3)
ENG-73109-B: Harden ingress edge to canonicalize or strip non-deterministic client headers by default; coordinate with platform networking team (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 2)
ENG-73109-C: Fix version-pinning cleanup path to ensure pin metadata removed on rollback; add e2e test; include retroactive migration for flagged deployments (owner: Miguel Alvarez, estimate: 3)
ENG-73109-D: Add unit + fuzz tests for route-hash function covering non-ASCII and unusual base64 variants; integrate into CI gating for rollouts (owner: Emily Tran, estimate: 2)

ENG-73109-E: Create an automatic rollout anomaly detector that compares observed vs configured traffic splits and pauses rollouts on >15% divergence for >2 minutes (owner: SRE oncall rotation, estimate: 5)
ENG-73109-F: Run a capacity verification test for dedicated pools to ensure graceful overload handling and fallback routing (owner: Performance team, estimate: 3)
ENG-73109-G: Postmortem review with affected customers and update incident communications template (owner: Carlos Mendes, assignee: Customer Success, estimate: 1)
ENG-73109-H: Document allowed header encodings in API contract and include automated enforcement in API gateway (owner: API team, estimate: 2)
notes: We chose strip-via-edge as a fast mitigation because it had the least blast radius. The long-term canonicalization must be coordinated with partners who rely on X-Client-Meta. Security has reviewed payload handling and confirmed no sensitive data was present in the header.
communication_plan: Notify affected customers with RCA and mitigation summary by 2026-03-16. Share postmortem in engineering all-hands on 2026-03-22.
